title: RFK Jr. goes full anti-vaccine bananas over two measles deaths—one was a newborn
gist: Following Pennsylvania's first measles deaths in 35 years (including a newborn), HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. spread misinformation questioning the deaths' cause, amid a national measles resurgence that has hit nearly 2,800 cases in 2026 — the highest US total since 1991 — underscoring continued federal-level erosion of vaccine policy credibility.

insights.claim: The US has recorded nearly 2,800 measles cases in 2026, the highest annual total since 1991, with Pennsylvania's outbreak alone reaching nearly 400 confirmed cases and producing the state's first measles deaths in 35 years.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: A 35-year high in US measles cases is a concrete, quantifiable public-health deterioration metric directly tied to declining vaccination rates, relevant to tracking outbreak-driven demand shifts for vaccine manufacturers and public health system strain.
insights.quote: The US has tallied nearly 2,800 cases so far this year, the highest total since 1991.

insights.claim: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. used his official US health secretary X account to allege the two Pennsylvania measles deaths 'may even have been altogether fabricated,' citing a local county commissioner's claim of 'zero measles deaths,' before local news and the county coroner clarified the cause-of-death details.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Documents the sitting US health secretary using his official capacity to spread doubt about confirmed vaccine-preventable-disease deaths, a continuing credibility and policy-risk factor for federal public health guidance and vaccine mandate enforcement broadly.
insights.quote: The deaths may even have been altogether fabricated by one of the Governor's hopeful staffers.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'On Wednesday, as news broke'

insights.claim: Vaccine expert Paul Offit (Children's Hospital of Philadelphia) said that, based on information from state officials, the newborn and second patient 'would not have died were it not for measles,' directly contradicting Kennedy's fabrication claims and the county coroner's initial non-committal statement.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: An independent medical expert directly rebuts the misinformation from the sitting health secretary, reinforcing the credibility gap between political messaging and clinical assessment on vaccine-preventable disease deaths.
insights.quote: These patients would not have died were it not for measles.

insights.claim: The author documents this as part of a repeated pattern by Kennedy and allies, citing a prior 2025 case in the Texas measles outbreak where Kennedy's advisor Robert Malone first announced then retracted a measles death claim, blaming pre-existing conditions instead, a claim the treating doctors refuted.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Establishes a recurring, documented pattern of cause-of-death misinformation from Kennedy's circle around vaccine-preventable disease outbreaks, useful context for assessing the credibility risk of future federal statements during outbreak events.
